n3d.blocket-som-ett-lopande-band.1: The block as an assembly line
n3d.blocket-som-ett-lopande-band.2: Inside each block, six things happen in a fixed order, like stations on an assembly line. Nothing runs at the same time: the MLP waits for attention, because it processes what attention has fetched.
n3d.attention-i-klartext.2: Attention is the model’s way of letting words gather information from other words. It works roughly like a search, with one important difference: you do not get a single hit, but a mix of all of them, weighted by how well they match.
n3d.attention-i-klartext.3: InputEach word’s vector, normalized. At this point the vector mostly knows about its own word.
n3d.attention-i-klartext.4:
Process 1. Each word makes three new vectors, each with its own learned matrix: a query (what am I looking for?), a key (what can I offer?) and a value (what do I pass on?).
2. The word’s query is compared with the key of every earlier word. The more they point the same way, the higher the score.
3. The scores become percentages that add up to 100 %.
4. The word takes a mix of all the values, weighted by the percentages. Nothing is filtered out entirely, but a poor match gets a very small weight.
n3d.attention-i-klartext.5: ResultA contribution per word that is added to its vector. Now the word knows something about its context.
n3d.attention-i-klartext.6: WhyThis is the only place in the whole model where words can affect each other. Without attention, every word would be handled in complete isolation.
n3d.attention-i-klartext.7: Analogy: searching among videos. Choose a query view; the first looks for what “{{example_pronoun}}” refers to. This uses whole words and handcrafted weights; each query sees only its own and earlier rows.
n3d.attention-formeln-bit-for.1: The attention formula, piece by piece
n3d.attention-formeln-bit-for.2: The whole attention step fits in one line. Click each part to see what it does, why it is there, and which numbers it gives in our worked example from “Attention worked out by hand”.
n3d.mlp-i-klartext.2: Attention has gathered information. The MLP works out what it means. It handles one word at a time and works roughly like a big reference book: if it recognizes a pattern, it adds what it knows about it.
n3d.mlp-i-klartext.3: InputOne word’s vector after attention, normalized: 4096 numbers that now carry context.
n3d.mlp-i-klartext.4:
Process 1. Expansion. The vector is compared with 14 336 learned patterns, one per neuron. In Llama that is done with two matrices in parallel: gate (does it match the pattern?) and up (how much should be passed on?).
2. Activation. SiLU on the gate works like a dimmer: neurons whose pattern matches are let through, the rest are damped almost to zero.
3. Projection. A third matrix, down, translates the neurons that lit up back into 4096 numbers.
n3d.mlp-i-klartext.5: ResultA contribution that is added to the word’s vector: what the model “knows” about what was fetched.
n3d.mlp-i-klartext.6: Why non-linear?Without the dimmer, the three matrices would be just one matrix, and the model could not make decisions of the kind “if A and B, but not C”.
